Command: Do no work on the Day of Atonement
Summary: On the Day of Atonement, no manner of work may be done; it is a sabbath of rest.
Commandment: On the Day of Atonement, do no manner of work.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The strictest work ban of the year matched the strictest holiness of the day. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
